input: Prepare me for a meeting with Datadog (datadoghq.com)

what_they_do.value: Datadog calls itself "AI-Powered Observability and Security" that lets customers "See inside any stack, any app, at any scale, anywhere."

priorities.priority: Building its own AI models and AI agents for operations (Bits AI and Scout)
priorities.evidence: In Q3 Datadog launched Scout 1.0, its AI Research team's first specialized model for investigating production issues. Scout is in Preview and now powers Bits Investigation. Datadog says it matches frontier models at a much lower inference cost. On the call, management called Bits AI the fastest-adopted product in company history. Bits testing became generally available in October, and Bits pricing moved to AI credits.

priorities.priority: 'Datadog for AI': monitoring, securing and tracking the cost of customers' AI agents, LLMs and GPUs
priorities.evidence: Q3 call figures: GPU devices monitored grew about 8x year to date. Agent observability span volume grew about 9x. AI cost tracking in Cloud Cost Management grew more than 11x. AI Guard protects custom agents at runtime. Datadog has more than 850 AI customers, up from about 750 last quarter, and about a third of all customers use at least one AI product. It is sold through the Anthropic marketplace and is a launch partner for OpenAI's enterprise marketplace.

priorities.priority: Agentic operations and data control, announced at DASH 2026
priorities.evidence: At DASH 2026 Datadog added Bits Agent Builder for automated remediation (with ServiceNow and Jira connections), Agent Console to monitor AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot), Bits Detection, Agent Evals, AI Guard, and BYOC Logs, which keeps log data in the customer's own cloud storage for data residency. CPO Yanbing Li said the goal is to give companies "operational control around these systems."

priorities.priority: Investing heavily in go-to-market, including federal and international markets
priorities.evidence: CFO David Obstler said Datadog is investing aggressively in go-to-market and scaling quota capacity. In Q3 it won a 5-year deal worth seven figures a year with a U.S. federal defense agency after earning FedRAMP High. Two of Japan's largest banks signed deals worth seven figures a year. The Q4 margin guide includes heavy marketing spend, including AWS re:Invent.

priorities.priority: Selling more products to existing customers
priorities.evidence: As of Q3 2026, 61% of customers use 4 or more products and 16% use 10 or more (up from 8%). Infrastructure Monitoring passed $2B in ARR and is growing in the mid-30s%. Trailing 12-month net revenue retention is in the low 120s%.

challenges.challenge: Its largest customer cut usage, and revenue depends heavily on that one account
challenges.evidence: Obstler said the largest customer "reduced their usage in the third quarter." It is still above its minimum commitment, but Q4 guidance assumes it spends only the minimum. Excluding that customer, implied Q4 growth is in the low-to-mid 30s%.

challenges.challenge: Growth guided to slow sharply, and the stock fell despite the beat
challenges.evidence: Q4 revenue guidance is $1.19–$1.20B, about 25–26% year-over-year growth, versus 35% in Q3. Datadog beat consensus (revenue $1.197B vs $1.14B expected; adjusted EPS $0.81 vs $0.64), yet shares fell about 12.5% premarket, from $220.52 to $192.99.

challenges.challenge: Early renewals by AI-native customers are cutting near-term revenue, and usage-based revenue is hard to predict
challenges.evidence: Several large AI-native customers renewed early at higher commitments but lower unit prices. Pomel said these renewals "do create, like, headwind into the short term into the revenue." Management said the fast-scaling AI cohort makes quarter-to-quarter revenue hard to model, and Q4 is also hit by year-end code freezes.

recent_changes.headline: Q3 2026 results: revenue $1.20B (+35% YoY), Q4 guided to $1.19–$1.20B
recent_changes.summary: Q3 revenue was $1.20B, up 35% from $885.7M. Non-GAAP operating income was $334M (28% margin), GAAP operating income $75M (6% margin), and free cash flow $251M. About 4,860 customers have $100k+ ARR, up 20%. FY2026 revenue guidance is $4.515–$4.525B.

recent_changes.headline: Scout 1.0, Datadog's first in-house specialized AI model
recent_changes.summary: Built by Datadog AI Research to investigate production issues. It is in Preview and powers Bits Investigation at lower inference cost than frontier models.

recent_changes.headline: Named a Leader in the 2026 Forrester Wave for AIOps Platforms
recent_changes.summary: Second year in a row as a Leader. Gartner's 2026 AI Vendor Race report also called Datadog the "Company to Beat" in observability platforms. Both were reported in the Q3 release.

recent_changes.headline: Bits testing generally available; Bits pricing moves to AI credits
recent_changes.summary: Disclosed on the Q3 earnings call.

recent_changes.headline: Shares fall about 12.5% premarket after the Q3 report
recent_changes.summary: Investors focused on the softer Q4 outlook and the guidance assuming the largest customer spends only its contractual minimum.

key_people.name: Olivier Pomel
key_people.title: Co-founder and CEO
key_people.recent: On the Nov 4, 2026 call he said "All 15 of the top 15 AI leaders are our customers," highlighted the AI Research team's specialized models (Scout), and acknowledged that early AI renewals create short-term revenue headwinds.

key_people.name: David Obstler
key_people.title: CFO
key_people.recent: Guided Q4 assuming the largest customer spends only its minimum commitment, said any spend above that would be "an implicit beat," and said Datadog is investing aggressively in go-to-market capacity.

key_people.name: Yanbing Li
key_people.title: Chief Product Officer
key_people.recent: Presented the DASH 2026 agentic launches (Bits Agent Builder, Agent Console, AI Guard, BYOC Logs) and framed the goal as giving companies "operational control around these systems."

talking_points: Scout is your own model, built to beat frontier models on inference cost. What outside data does Bits need that you don't get from customers' own telemetry, and how do you source it today?

AI customers grew from about 750 to more than 850 in one quarter, and agent span volume is up about 9x. As you sell Agent Console and AI Guard, which gaps in agent workflows (web access, tool calls, external data) are customers asking you to cover?

With Q4 guided to 25–26% growth and the largest customer at its minimum commitment, what is the bar for new spend right now? Does it need to support growth outside AI-native customers or reduce costs?
